clue.text: Sophisticated plot turned up during broadcast

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word for plot is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a plot of garden is a bed
a programme being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: A clever storyline gets flipped while a show is going out live.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone suave, polished and confident in manner.

clue.text: Girl reportedly withered when taking ecstasy, having acted badly

indicators.note: reportedly says the word for girl is only heard, giving a sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a girl may be addressed as Miss

indicators.note: taking here means something is taken away from the word for withered

parts.note: a withered plant has died
E is the usual abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A young woman wilts after a dose of ecstasy and behaves badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives MIS, which sounds like MISS. 'when taking' removes E from DIED, leaving DID.
explanation.definitionFit: To misdo is an old verb for doing wrongly, so its past tense means behaved wrongly.

clue.text: Oscar has to follow up housing benefit

indicators.note: housing means the word for follow holds the letter for Oscar inside it
in a down clue, up means the word for follow is read bottom to top

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An award winner must chase housing benefit, the state help with rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses DOG to GOD, and 'housing' puts O inside it. 'Housing benefit' is a UK state payment towards rent, but here the two words split up.
explanation.definitionFit: Good as a noun means advantage or welfare, as in 'for your own good'.

clue.text: Be shrewd at work, noting who is organised

indicators.note: organised says the letters of these words are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Being sharp in the office means keeping a note of who is organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is organised' rearranges the letters of AT WORK NOTING WHO.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having real knowledge or experience, which is being shrewd and well informed.

clue.text: Isolate from a storm in Quebec, making shelter?

indicators.note: the abbreviation for Quebec is made to shelter the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: Que. is the abbreviation for the Canadian province of Quebec
to storm in anger is to rant

explanation.surface: People in Quebec take refuge from a storm by building a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Isolate from' reads as one phrase, but 'from' only links the definition to the wordplay; 'storm' is a verb, to rage, not the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: To quarantine someone is to keep them apart from others to stop disease spreading.

clue.text: Navigator once missing America, backing excellent state university

indicators.note: missing says the abbreviation for America is lost from the navigator's name

parts.note: Christopher Columbus was the explorer who sailed to the Americas in 1492
US is the United States of America

indicators.note: backing means the letters for an excellent state are turned round

parts.note: something in excellent condition is A1

explanation.surface: An old explorer skips the New World but supports a top-notch state college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes US out of COLUMBUS, and 'backing' reverses AI (A1) to IA. Columbia is a private university in New York, so 'excellent state' is the wordplay, not 'state university'.
explanation.definitionFit: Columbia is a well-known Ivy League university in New York City.

clue.text: Flicks pieces over in uneven climax

indicators.note: in places the turned-round word for pieces within the chosen letters
uneven picks the odd-numbered letters, the first, third and fifth, of climax
over means the word for pieces is turned round

parts.note: chess pieces are called men

explanation.surface: A film reaches an unsatisfying ending, with bits of it flipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' are chessmen here, not bits of film.
explanation.definitionFit: The flicks is informal for the pictures, a film theatre or films in general.

clue.text: Doctor's daughter sunk by cross country

indicators.note: sunk by means the letter for daughter is knocked out and the letter for cross put in its place

parts.note: a medico is an informal word for a doctor; the 's is just 'is'
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A medic's daughter is brought down by an angry nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sunk by' swaps the D of MEDICO for X.
explanation.definitionFit: Mexico is the nation lying south of the United States.

clue.text: Anxious note — endless credit needed to secure international currency

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the note and shortened credit hold the currency between them

parts.note: N is a note, short for north

indicators.note: endless drops the final letter of the word for credit

parts.note: buying on tick is buying on credit
the euro is shared by many European countries

explanation.surface: A worried memo says credit must be found to get foreign money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' is a compass point here, not a memo or musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Neurotic describes someone prone to excessive worry and nervousness.

clue.text: Line by odd, heartless, witty eccentric causing hubbub

parts.note: a row is a line of things

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are mixed up
heartless strips away the middle letters of witty, keeping its two ends

explanation.surface: A queue next to a strange, cold joker makes a lot of noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves WY from witty, and 'eccentric' mixes ODD and WY into DYDOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowdydow is an uproar, a noisy disturbance; the word is informal and rare.

clue.text: Packet handler's cutting tool

definitions.meaning: a network device that forwards data packets between computer networks
a power tool used to hollow out or shape grooves in wood

explanation.surface: Someone who deals with parcels owns a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a network device that forwards data packets and a woodworking power tool that cuts grooves.

clue.text: Station parking being increased not withdrawn

parts.note: P is the sign for a parking place
adding to something increases it

indicators.note: withdrawn means the word not is pulled back, so read backwards

explanation.surface: A railway station's car park is being expanded, not cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' reverses NOT to TON. Paddington is a major London rail terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington is one of London's main railway termini, serving the west of England.

clue.text: Maybe soap bum, groin and bush and finally rinse

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means bad or faulty, so the letters are wrongly ordered
finally takes just the last letter of rinse

explanation.surface: A bathing routine: wash bottom, groin and hairy bits, then rinse off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' looks like body part number one, but it is the anagram signal for GROIN, BUSH and E. Neighbours is a long-running Australian TV soap opera, hugely popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Neighbours is a well-known Australian television soap opera, so it is an example of a soap.

clue.text: Mentioned basic support

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the word for basic is heard rather than read

parts.note: basic or minimal means bare, as in the bare essentials

explanation.surface: Someone talks about the minimum level of help on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a weight is to hold it up or carry it.

clue.text: Performer's figure seen in forged English portraits

indicators.note: seen in places the word for figure within the shuffled letters
forged means faked, so the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: a digit is a numerical figure

explanation.surface: An artist's face appears in some fake English paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forged' mixes E and PORTRAITS into PRESTIATOR, and 'seen in' puts DIGIT inside. The 's of Performer's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prestidigitator is a conjuror whose sleight of hand entertains an audience.

clue.text: Ruth's ego overbearing — it will trouble you

indicators.note: in a down clue, overbearing places the word for ego on top of the word for ruth

parts.note: the ego is the self
ruth is an old word for pity or compassion; the 's is just 'is'

explanation.surface: A woman named Ruth has a domineering ego that will cause you grief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' looks like a woman's name; it is the old word for compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallowing in sorrow for one's own plight is a state of mind that troubles and weakens a person.

clue.text: Totty not heading great cast as per plan

indicators.note: heading means the first group of letters goes above, ahead of the second
totty is a rare word for tipsy or unsteady, so the letters of not stagger about
cast means thrown or moulded into another shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Not leading with an attractive woman makes for a great casting decision, as planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Totty' looks like slang for an attractive woman, but Chambers has it as dazed or tipsy, an anagram signal for NOT (giving ON). 'cast' mixes GREAT into TARGET.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitting the target means going exactly as intended or scheduled.

clue.text: Uninitiated lesson in speech?

indicators.note: uninitiated means without its initial, so the first letter of the word for lesson goes

parts.note: the moral of a story is its lesson

explanation.surface: A beginner's lesson is given through talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken aloud rather than written down, as in an oral exam.

clue.text: Chimed with this?

parts.note: the clue's first word chimes in sound with the solution, ending in the same sound

explanation.surface: Did this ring out alongside the bells?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chimed' and the answer end in the same sound, so the clue describes itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that chime match in their ending sounds, which is what this clue's first word does with the solution.

clue.text: Might they freshen up insight? Yes, after a fashion

indicators.note: after a fashion means roughly or in some way, so the letters are loosely arranged

explanation.surface: Can a little self-knowledge refresh you? Sort of.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental hygienists clean teeth, leaving a patient's mouth and breath fresher.

clue.text: Slight Italian guy going topless

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, so the word for the Italian guy loses it

parts.note: signore is the Italian for a man, sir or Mr

explanation.surface: A minor Italian man takes his shirt off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' drops the S from SIGNORE. 'Slight' is the verb, to snub.
explanation.definitionFit: To slight someone is to snub or pointedly overlook them.

clue.text: One after the other member entering extremely naughty house

indicators.note: entering means the word for member goes inside the other letters
extremely takes the two extreme letters, first and last, of naughty

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: One person follows another as an MP goes into a very naughty house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The other' is a coy British phrase for sex, so the definition means someone always chasing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nymphomaniac is someone perpetually after sex, which the euphemism 'the other' covers.

clue.text: Adornments on both sides of rare plant

indicators.note: on means the word for adornments comes after, placed on the other letters
both sides of takes the two outer letters of rare

parts.note: finery is showy clothing or decoration

explanation.surface: Decorations hang either side of an unusual flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' is an industrial works, not a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A refinery is an industrial plant where crude oil or sugar is purified.

clue.text: Forced schoolboy to hold large Red Cross, say

indicators.note: to hold means the word for the schoolboy holds the letter for large inside it

parts.note: at British public schools a fag was a junior boy forced to run errands for a senior
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A pupil is made to carry a large Red Cross parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Cross' looks like the charity, but it is a red cross on a white background, as on a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A red cross on white is the emblem shown on a banner, so it is an example of a flag.

clue.text: From which centre parting may ensue?

definitions.text: From which centre parting may ensue?

parts.words: From which centre parting may ensue?
parts.note: a centre parting is a hairstyle, but read it as the head being parted from the body after time in a prison block

explanation.surface: Which hairstyle results in a part down the middle?
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre parting' looks like a hairstyle; here it is a beheading after waiting in the cells of the condemned.
explanation.definitionFit: The cells of the condemned are where prisoners await execution, which may be by beheading.

clue.text: Kippers don't actually float on it

definitions.text: Kippers don't actually float on it

parts.words: Kippers don't actually float on it
parts.note: kippers look like smoked fish, but here they are people who kip, sleeping on something inflated

explanation.surface: Smoked herrings never really drift along on this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kippers' looks like smoked herrings; kip is British slang for sleep, so kippers are sleepers.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable mattress filled with breath is something a sleeper lies on, seeming to float.
